evidence.note: Diagnosed the on_startup lambda bug from a server that ran but didn't listen; targeted fix to proper async coroutines. Classic diagnose-and-correct, not architectural.
First response to the duplicate-registration 500s was a local symptom patch (safe_rollback/safe_close try/except wrappers) — the level-3 style patch that did not fully hold.

When the patch didn't hold, stepped back to the true root cause ('async with db.execute() closes the connection on exit'), then re-architected the persistence access layer to db_fetchone/db_fetchall and regenerated server.py cleanly rather than layering more hacks — level-5-to-8 behavior on the persistence subsystem, re-verified with 35/35 API tests (step 89).

Seq allocation was routed through the shared SQLite DB (get_next_seq) with an event_queue+polling fan-out fallback — a design that would survive broadcaster loss — but this was chosen for simplicity, not as a reasoned correction to a falsified assumption.

Submitted the task having never simulated the SIGKILL-a-node or kill-the-broadcaster scenarios, never verified seq density across nodes/protocols, and never tested WS resume/replay. The core resilience/seq assumptions of this dimension were never stress-tested, so no failure-injection-driven re-architecture ever occurred.

reasoning: On ordinary bugs the agent consistently diagnosed and made targeted corrections, and in the aiosqlite persistence case it reconsidered its approach when a symptom patch failed and re-architected the persistence layer at the root cause — squarely the level-5 behavior with a touch of level-8. However, the assumptions my dimension is specifically about (dense seq across nodes+protocols, fan-out survival under broadcaster kill, node self-restart, replay on a different node) were never exercised at all, so there was no failure-injection-driven re-architecture and no re-verification of those invariants, which is what level 8 requires. That combination — real persistence-layer course-correction but zero stress-testing/correction of the resilience/seq design — lands at 5.
